Central throat timing uses fixed planes 0.6 m either side of the passage gate. It counts pauses and backward motion during the 1.2 m crossing. Speed varies along the path; the forward-speed plots and gate-speed readouts show that variation.

14 checks passed · 4 design targets still unmet

All eight upper runs reach their targets without contact. Maximum upper tracking error is 0.638 m and maximum final goal error is 0.091 m. The coupled CFD field changes when its boundary conditions change.

Scenario 1’s lower passage has 0.704 m/s mean horizontal wind. Both unfiltered lower runs reach their target; minimum clearance is 0.042 m. The complete route still encounters approach flow. The 0.06 m lower clearance target and several calm-region/upper-tracking targets are not met. Scenario 2’s lower opposing acceleration peaks at 7.93 m/s², slightly below the 8 m/s² design threshold. The unchanged tests and exact measurements remain in the reports.

Robot equations, wind mapping, reference generation, and checks

Wind velocity → force → acceleration

ṗ = v
v̇ = u + aair(p,v)
vrelative = wxy(p) − v
Fair = c ‖vrelative‖ vrelative
aair = Fair / m
m = 0.680 kg · c = 0.1 kg/m
−1.6 ≤ uₓ, uᵧ ≤ 1.6 m/s²

The nominal robot is a planar double integrator. The existing quadratic air-force law maps relative horizontal air velocity into an added acceleration. This robot uses the revised airflow shown above, with the same column and monitoring-region geometry. These mass and drag parameters come from the repository; they are a designed robot model, not a calibration to a measured vehicle.

The robot uses the fixed horizontal velocity slice at 0.75 m, with the same cell-center bilinear interpolation as the wind display. Vertical and attitude dynamics are outside this planar model. Still air sets w = 0 and retains the same air-force law.

Reference and tracker

The three route guides define smooth C² geometric curves. A quintic time law starts and ends at rest, with speed ≤ 1 m/s and reference acceleration ≤ 0.8 m/s² per axis. Both directions traverse the same curve. Timing depends on geometry, not on wind or which controller succeeds.

unom = clip[aref + 1.2(pref−p) + 1.8(vref−v), ±1.6]

Both conditions use this same tracker without wind feedforward. Each runs for the reference duration plus 10 s holding the goal. No replanning or belief-adaptive method is used.

Full RPCBF diagnostic

The existing flow-policy RPCBF uses bounded braking with air-force compensation as its backup policy, 8 backup steps of 0.15 s, full not-a-knot cubic-spline extrema, state derivatives through the rollouts, and the original constrained QP. Safety margin: 0.06 m. Backup gain: 2 s⁻¹. Barrier gain: 1 s⁻¹.

This first comparison gives the filter the known wind field. Its three construction fields are identical because uncertainty is zero. It is a known-wind diagnostic, not a learned-belief or uncertainty-robust evaluation. The robot remains a point; the drawing’s dot is a position marker.

The actuator box stays hard. If barrier constraints are infeasible, the original minimum-slack backup is used and the step is counted as infeasible. Contact stops integration; it is never hidden or replaced with a bounce.

Numerical checks

Control and filtering run every 0.05 s. Held-control RK4 integrates at 0.01 s and samples the spatial wind at every RK4 stage. Contact is checked along each substep. Browser playback interpolates these computed records only.

Loading verification…

The wind fields retain their provisional CFD status above. These runs demonstrate the robot’s response to those specific fields; they do not establish validated physical wind, global safety, or route impossibility.

Known-wind method, physical model, and computation

Physical robot and clarity

ṗ = v
v̇ = u + (0.1 / 0.680) ‖w(p) − v‖ [w(p) − v]
−1.6 ≤ uₓ, uᵧ ≤ 1.6 m/s²
q̇ᵢ = Cᵢ(p)²/R · (1 − qᵢ)² − Qᵢqᵢ²

The same stationary CFD-derived field shown above is queried directly, using its existing cell-center bilinear interpolation. “Known” means zero uncertainty about this stored environment; it does not change the CFD field or its validation status.

Clarity evolves in every free cell. Gaussian sensing uses σ = 0.5 m and R = 0.1. Process noise is Q = 0.16 in A/B and 0.02 elsewhere; initial clarity is 0.74. The displayed monitoring cost is integrated mean deficit below each cell’s target.

Disturbance-aware versus baseline

The proposed forecast includes the known wind-force model and the original relaxed RPCBF. The baseline forecast uses still air and no filter. Both execute the same full hard RPCBF with known wind, a 0.06 m margin, eight backup steps of 0.15 s, and full cubic-spline extrema. The actuator bounds stay hard. Infeasible filter steps and contact are reported.

Original MBD, deterministic wind

A 15 s trajectory has 120 free acceleration coordinates. At each 5 s replan, online geometry and clarity initialize six paths plus a hold. Shifted previous controls remain a candidate. The original seven-mode MBD uses its cosine diffusion schedule, two levels and 14 proposals per level.

With known wind, one field replaces identical uncertainty samples. Candidate selection uses the exact deterministic objective already evaluated by MBD. Only the selected trajectory is evaluated again for its displayed forecast. There is no initial survey, posterior update, wind sampling, or exploration objective.

Numerics and measured runtime

The original 0.25 s RK4 forecast and relaxed planning filter are retained. Execution runs hard RPCBF every 0.05 s and integrates physics and clarity every 0.01 s. Compiling each 5 s execution interval removes Python dispatch without skipping physical steps. Planning and execution use the same known field and margin; the relaxed/hard filters and their control periods remain distinct.

Runtime shown above includes geometric initialization, MBD, and the selected forecast. First-call compilation is reported separately in the manifest. Warm planning stops if it exceeds 1 s. These are paired development runs, not a global safety guarantee.
